key_insight: An AI-driven design pipeline identified four novel bimetallic HER catalyst candidates with DFT-validated near-thermoneutral hydrogen binding: Pd5Au, Pt5Rh, Cu5Pt3, and Pd13Ru3.
engineering_relevance: Combining generative design with surrogate screening can prioritize alloy compositions and surface structures for costly DFT evaluation and experimental follow-up.
method: Fine-tune MatterGen on adsorption-labelled bulk alloys to generate novel binaries targeting near-zero hydrogen adsorption energy.
Use MatterSim to screen surface stability and relax hydrogen-adsorbed slabs at high-symmetry sites.
Shortlist candidates using MEGNet–ALIGNN consensus and MatterSim energy differences, then validate with DFT and phonon calculations.
evidence_signal: Of eight alloys evaluated with plane-wave DFT, four met the thermoneutral hydrogen-binding criterion; all eight were dynamically stable by phonon calculations.
watch_item: Experimental HER activity and durability remain unverified, and the four highlighted candidates contain precious metals despite the earth-abundance motivation.
paper_title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
